title: Buenas
desc: Four people between you and the pulpería, and none of them can be passed in silence
setting: It is seven in the morning and you have to walk the length of your own street.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.en: Morning, young man. How are you?

options.es: Buenas, don Beto. Bien, gracias. ¿Y usted?
options.en: Morning, don Beto. Fine, thanks. And you?
options.feedback: His name, the don, and the question back. To a man of seventy the usted is not optional.
You greeted him, which is the main thing. It is short for a neighbour who has known you a month.
Vos to a man that age. He will answer you anyway and he will file it away.

options.en: Not yet, doña. I am just heading out.
options.feedback: She is not really asking about breakfast. Answering the question and saying where you are going is the whole exchange.
Perfectly fine. It closes the conversation a little faster than she wanted.
Nobody is checking up on you. Have you eaten is a greeting here, not an enquiry.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.en: What is up? Where are you off to?

options.feedback: Vos back to a chavalo of twelve is exactly right, and the question back is what turns a greeting into a conversation.

options.en: I am going to the pulpería.
options.feedback: True, and a bit flat. He asked partly so you would ask him.
He is twelve. Señor will make him laugh at you for a week.
Adiós shouted across a street is a greeting, not a goodbye. It is what you say to somebody you are not going to stop for.
Understood everywhere and never wrong. Adiós would have matched her exactly.
You heard it as a farewell and explained yourself. She was only saying hello from her door.
